biography.bio1: Since she was little, she attended several workshops where she began to develop her style, starting with portraiture.
biography.bio2: At 19, she began pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Visual Arts at the National University of the Arts (Buenos Aires), ultimately choosing to major in Painting. Her time at the university was significant, as she was able to experiment with other disciplines such as sculpture and installation.
biography.bio3: She also attended workshops with renowned artists, such as Adriana Cerviño's ceramics workshop and painting workshops with Lean Frizzera and Ricardo Celma.
biography.bio4: At the same time, she began tattooing as a self-taught artist at the age of 19 and, since 2019, has had her own tattoo studio in Buenos Aires.

home.aboutText1: My work stems from a displacement: the feeling of being disconnected from nature and, simultaneously, from my own body. I work from this place of tension, exploring how cultural systems—patriarchy, capitalism, and urban life—shape our perception of the natural, the feminine, and the instinctive.
home.aboutText2: Through painting, sculpture, and tattooing, I develop images where the female body merges, resists, or transforms in relation to its environment. I am interested in representing non-hegemonic bodies, vulnerable yet powerful; bodies that escape domestication and approach the wild as a form of freedom. My practice is deeply influenced by ecofeminism, understanding the connection between the exploitation of nature and the oppression of feminized bodies. At this intersection, questions about belonging, identity, and memory emerge: what does it mean to return to nature when we have been historically separated from it? Water, earth, animals, and landscapes function as symbols of transformation, loss, and resistance. In them, I project both contemporary anxiety and the possibility of reconnection. My work does not seek to provide answers but to open spaces for reflection on how we inhabit our bodies and the world.
